description: A department head must finalize the format and participation rules for a team offsite intended to rebuild working relationships after a difficult reorganization.

shared_context.S1: The team has scheduled an offsite to improve collaboration after a difficult reorganization.
shared_context.S2: Priya makes the final decision about the offsite format, facilitator, and participation rules.
shared_context.S3: Morgan, an internal manager who often facilitates team exercises, has been suggested as the offsite facilitator.
shared_context.S4: As part of the department's normal event-planning process, Priya asks each attendee and HR to state relevant constraints or preferences before finalizing the plan.

PF1.text: Evan has sole caregiving responsibilities that prevent him from staying overnight and require him to leave any in-person event by 4:00 p.m.; he has not raised this because the offsite invitation did not yet include a detailed schedule.

PF2.text: Rosa previously had a serious unresolved conflict with Morgan and will participate in the offsite only if an external neutral facilitator is used and she is not paired with Morgan for an exercise; she has not discussed this with Priya because she expected the facilitator choice to be made later.

PF3.text: Maya confirmed that HR policy requires a live remote alternative for any team-building event and requires participation to be opt-in without requiring employees to disclose personal reasons; she has not yet added this requirement to the event plan.

acceptance_conditions: The offsite must be a one-day in-person event ending by 4:00 p.m. with no overnight stay.
An external neutral facilitator must be selected.
Rosa must not be paired with Morgan for an exercise.
A live remote alternative must be offered.
Participation must be opt-in and employees must not be required to give a personal reason.
The settlement must record the relevant private information as a basis for the decision.

content_checks.C1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and decisions['in_person_end_time_hour'] == 16 and decisions['overnight_stay'] == False
content_checks.C3: 'PF2' in credited_facts and decisions['facilitator'] in ['external neutral facilitator', 'External neutral facilitator', 'external neutral facilitator (not Morgan)', 'External neutral facilitator (not Morgan)']
content_checks.C4: 'PF2' in credited_facts and any(c['target'] == 'Rosa' and 'Morgan' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C5: 'PF3' in credited_facts and ('live remote' in decisions['remote_alternative'] or 'Live remote' in decisions['remote_alternative']) and decisions['participation_opt_in'] == True and decisions['personal_reason_required'] == False

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed
provenance_checks.P3: 'PF3' in credited_facts and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Without Evan's caregiving constraint, the default offsite could include an overnight stay or continue past 4:00 p.m.; his fact fixes the in-person end time at hour 16 and requires no overnight stay.
Without Rosa's specific prior conflict with Morgan, there is no basis to replace the suggested internal facilitator with an external neutral facilitator or prohibit pairing Rosa with Morgan.

Without Maya's confirmed HR rule, the plan could omit a live remote alternative, allow mandatory participation, or require an explanation for nonparticipation; her fact changes those choices to live remote access, opt-in participation, and no personal-reason requirement.
